observation.visible_scene: A clear, rounded cylindrical glass sits centered on a pale marbled surface against a uniform blue backdrop, with a faint reflection of the glass base on the surface. The glass is already largely filled with white milk, topped by a foamy surface. A continuous stream of white milk pours into the glass from above, entering at a diagonal angle near the top center/right of the rim. The composition, glass position, background, and surface remain fixed across all frames, indicating a stationary camera.
visible_changes: The pouring stream is present and active throughout the entire excerpt; it neither begins nor ends within the segment.
The milk level inside the glass rises only very gradually, staying near the upper portion of the glass the whole time.

The foamy surface deforms over time: the rounded foam mound/bulge to the right of the stream entry shifts in shape and merges more smoothly into the surface line in later frames, and the foam texture along the surface changes subtly.
The stream column wavers slightly in angle and thickness frame to frame, and its point of contact with the surface moves a little left/right.
The glass, background, surface, and reflection show no positional change, so the observed motion is fluid motion, not camera or object translation.
outside_clip_unknowns: When the pouring started and when it will stop are not shown.
The source/container of the milk and any operator are unseen.
Whether the glass will overflow or the level will reach the rim is not determined by the excerpt.
uncertain_details: The exact rate of level rise is small and hard to quantify between frames.
Apparent changes in stream shape may partly reflect foam interaction at the surface rather than a change in the stream itself.
Camera is treated as static because background and glass position are constant, but no parallax evidence confirms this definitively.
